Match their chunky, stepped pixel blocks, dark warm near-black outlines, muted cream/bone, rust brown, antique brass and charcoal steel palette, and upper-left highlights. Single complete isolated creature/object, three-quarter battle view toward screen left, no environment or ground shadow. It should look drawn at roughly 112x140 logical pixels and enlarged with nearest-neighbor to about 1120x1400: hard square 10px blocks, 1–2 block outline, approximately 3–7 broad shade bands, no dithering or smooth shading. Use a small coherent palette (up to 32 colors). Fully transparent empty background, fully opaque sprite, no translucent effects or antialiased edges. No lettering, UI, border, watermark or labels. Do not add traits, props or weapons absent from the following source description. Weakness elements are metadata, not visual powers.
Source: design/enemies.json enemy burning_bloodline; name 불타는 혈통; family 20 잿불 신도; original grade core; art grade boss. Exact appearance (authoritative Korean): 혈통 시험에서 죽은 신관 후보들
Source actions for pose or explicitly named equipment only: 시험의 낙인, 혈통의 불, 시험의 불, 시험의 불길, 낙인 찍기.
ONE cohesive composite enemy sprite. Include exactly the multiple constituent figures or bodies stated in the source, fused or grouped as described; no lineup or separate variants. Keep the entire silhouette and all tips inside frame with generous transparent margins. No scenery, floor or detached background fragments. Any source inscriptions must be abstract tiny marks, never legible lettering. No new heraldry or invented decoration.
Faithful English translation of the source appearance: Candidates for the priesthood who died during the bloodline trial.
PRIORITY: The exact source subject and material override every reference subject. References show pixel technique only. Do not copy their puppet anatomy, brass armor, face plates, smoke vents, or accessories into an enemy that is not described with those features. Use the stated source anatomy and stated props visibly. All mandatory source props must be readable in the silhouette. No readable letters; source inscriptions are tiny abstract marks.
